messages.subject: !! May Institute 2018 - Computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics at Northeastern University in Boston
messages.subject_clean: !! May Institute 2018 - Computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics at Northeastern University in Boston
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats users:

I would like to share with you that the May Institute on computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics, taking place on April 30 – May 11, 2018 on campus of Northeastern University in Boston MA, is now accepting applications https://computationalproteomics.ccis.northeastern.edu/ The application deadline is January 31, 2018.

Participants can select a subset of the following modules:

April 30 – May 2, 2018 : Targeted proteomics with Skyline
April 30 – May 2, 2018 : Proteomics and metabolomics with OpenMS
May 2-4, 2018 : Beginner’s statistics in R
May 2-4, 2018 : Advanced R
May 7-9, 2018 : Statistics for quantitative mass spectrometry
May 7-9, 2018 : Visualization of biomolecular data
May 9-11, 2018 : Capstone – case studies in data-independent acquisition (DIA)

Instructors are leading experts in this field, who contributed numerous experimental and computational methods and software. The target audience are both beginners and experienced scientists, with both experimental and computational expertise.

Tuition fee wavers and travel fellowships will be available for students and postdocs affiliated with academic institutions in the US.

It is great opportunity for MSstats users to discuss with MSstats teams. Also there are more interesting topics for bench scientist and bioinformaticians. I look forward to seeing you at this course. Please share this information widely.

- Meena

messages.subject: DDA analysis with/without imputation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Meena,

I performed analysis of DDA data (Q-Exactive) in MSstats.

Unfortunately I have many missing data, so I was thought that is a good idea to use for analysis MSstats with imputation option. Results which I obtained with imputation are considerably different from that without imputation (there is only about 25% common differential proteins which fulfil p<0.05) and I do not know which analysis is better? Although imputation increases the number of proteins which are significant on the p value level, on the adjusted value level the number of protein is the same (there are a few  proteins with adjusted p-value<0.05).

QQplots and ResidualPlots are not obviously better in any case; for some proteins they are looking  better with the imputation option for other without the imputation. Additionally, manual supervision of all plots for about  6000 proteins  is difficult to implement.

Are there some tools in MSstats allowing an objective assessment of these two approaches?

I will be very grateful for your advice.

Best regards

Sylwia

messages.body_plain:
If you want to attend any of the sessions of the May institute - Computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics at NEU in 2018, now is the time to get your application in. The two-week course is divided into 2.5 day segments focusing on the computational and statistical aspects of quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics. The course offerings include keynote presentations, introductory or advanced lectures, tutorial training and informal personal discussions. Details are available in https://computationalproteomics.ccis.northeastern.edu/

The application <https://computationalproteomics.ccis.northeastern.edu/application/> deadline is Wednesday, January 31

It is great opportunity for MSstats users to discuss with MSstats teams. Also there are more interesting topics for bench scientist and bioinformaticians. Academic students and postdocs may also apply for a limited number of registration fee waivers and travel fellowships.

Hope you can join us.

- Meena

messages.subject: Re: DDA analysis with/without imputation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sylwia,

Unfortunately, MSstats does not have other functionality to compare the outputs with two different options.
One of the output of groupComparison, xxx$$ModelQC has two extra columns, residuals and fitted. You can check the normality with these values by protein.
Another output of groupComparison, xxx$fittedmodel is the list which include the fitted model by protein. You also can check it.

I think that you used MaxQuant output. (It is my guess, based on the dataset you shared last time for bug of model QC plots.) I tested several controlled mixture datasets by MaxQuant, which we know the truth. I confirmed that default option in MSstats, (imputation + TMP) provides the best performance for MaxQuant output.

I hope that it will be helpful.

- Meena

messages.subject: sample size calculation
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have done SRM-MS analysis of few targets, of which only one protein was significant after multiple hypothesis testing. The fold change of that protein is 0.85 (based on MSstat results which in log scale of -0.23), I have following questions.

1. The fold change of 0.85, is this a ratio?

2. My protein is down-regulated and the default setting for fold change is 1.25 to 1.75. In order to calculate future samples size for the decreased abundance of my protein, what range I should give for down-regulated protein?

Thanks, Santosh

2. You can change the range of fold change as you want. It also works with desired fold change less than 1. For example, you can set the desired fold change, (0.5, 1.5)

Hope to help.

- Meena
